# Portenv: full description for language models

> Portenv — your portable workspace (short for portable environment; also heard as 'port env'). Resume your work anywhere: an encrypted workspace that moves between your Mac and your own servers, and that your agents can join, on your terms.

Status: Available for Mac (macOS 26 or later, Apple silicon). Download: https://portenv.com/download

This text describes what the released app does. Each release's notes say what is in it: https://github.com/portenv/portenv/releases/latest

## Boxes

- Each project gets a box: a workspace with its files, history, tools and settings together.
- A box runs on your Mac or on a server you own. Move To takes it from one to another and picks up exactly where you left off.
- On the Mac, boxes run in Docker Desktop for now.
- A box saves as you go and works offline; saves go out when the network is back.
- You can make a save point before a risky change, and revert to it later. Reverting never throws away the work it replaces.

## Security

- Each box is encrypted on your device before it is saved, with keys kept in your Mac's Keychain.
- Only one machine has a box open at a time, so two copies never drift apart.
- Agents work inside a box but can never read its encryption keys or passwords.
- Portenv opens no public or inbound ports on your machines.

## Agents

Works with agents that run in a terminal, such as Claude Code, and with agents on their own computers over SSH (Preview, off until you turn it on).

- You invite an agent to one box. It continues your work in your own sessions.
- You see what each agent does, by name. You can revoke it at any time, and its access ends at once.
- When an agent connects, Portenv makes a save point, so you can undo everything it did.

## Open source

The runner, the in-box agent and the save format are Apache-2.0, at https://github.com/portenv/portenv. Portenv works with your own servers and storage, without a Portenv account.
